Scheduler for replaying FEC sets, parsing transactions, and managing staged fork blocks.

# Purpose
This file implements the `fd_sched` scheduler for block replay and transaction dispatch. It manages a tree of blocks, where each block tracks parsed transactions, execution and signature verification state, FEC buffer state, and fork relations to parent and child blocks. The scheduler accepts FEC sets, parses microblock and transaction data, expands address lookup tables when needed, and stores parsed transactions in an internal transaction pool. It also keeps metrics for block, lane, and transaction activity, plus counters for ingested, dropped, and parsed data.

The code also controls replay flow across staged and unstaged forks. It uses a dispatcher interface (`fd_rdisp`) to add, promote, remove, and abandon blocks and transactions, and it selects the next ready task with [`fd_sched_task_next_ready`](<#fd_sched_task_next_ready>). That task can be block start, block end, transaction execution, or transaction signature verification. The file defines the scheduler object layout, creation and join functions, root update and root notification logic, block abandonment, and helper routines that compute and stage the longest unstaged fork. It is a C implementation file that exposes public scheduler APIs and uses internal helpers to enforce state rules and replay order.
